probe_provenance: Initial runs used the same receive/pacing/CPU/RSS/scoring code as the committed probe; later additions only record probe/date/provider metadata, lazy-load optional dependencies, and reject empty input. The final committed probe was rerun successfully on both original language samples. Later input/output safety guards do not change measured audio, scoring or timing boundaries.
limitations: This is a regression corpus, not a representative accuracy estimate: 11 Mandarin clips/141 characters and 74 English clips/1180 words; limited speakers and domains.
No noisy-room, accent, mixed-language, Windows hardware, private microphone or paid API measurements.
Broader 85-clip variants each have one measured pass after warmup; small 10-clip bulk variants have two passes; paced variants one pass. Run order was sequential, not randomized.
Timing differences can reflect shared cloud scheduling; no general speed or memory improvement established. CPU-seconds are not electrical energy.
One-thread greedy changes three raw transcripts: one spelling/word-boundary tradeoff and two punctuation-only changes.
One-thread beam search improves normalized CER in seven clips and worsens two versus default two-thread greedy.
Peak memory is a process lifetime high-water mark, not per-utterance allocation or total system memory.
No runtime defaults changed. Optional correction-thinking behavior is verified offline only; no measured paid cost, quality or latency claim.
